reference: Kramida 2024, NIST Atomic Spectra Database (ver. 5.12), https://doi.org/10.18434/T4W30F
authors: A. Kramida, Yu. Ralchenko, J. Reader, and NIST ASD Team
title: NIST Atomic Spectra Database (ver. 5.12)
method: NIST critically evaluated compilation (see asd_compilation and asd_references for the original measurements)
uncertainty: per-level ASD uncertainties in column 'Uncertainty (cm-1)' (empty where ASD gives none)
conversion: Not exported, no single valence electron level: 66 rows (Li II (1s2 1S<0>) Limit ---, 1s.2s.2p 4P* 1/2, 1s.2s.2p 4P* 3/2, 1s.2s.2p 4P* 5/2, 1s.2p.(1P*).2s 2P* 1/2, 1s.2p.(1P*).2s 2P* 3/2, 1s.2p2 4P 1/2, 1s.2p2 4P 3/2, ...).

Energies from 'ground state 1s2.2s 2S 1/2', energy zero: ASD Li I output (compilation L7256, Kelly 1987 level list, 'not critically evaluated by NIST') does not state an isotope or hyperfine reference; levels are not isotope resolved. The adopted EI of Bushaw 2007 refers to the ground-state hfs centre of gravity.
caveats: Energies are term energies in cm^-1 relative to the ASD ground state 1s2.2s 2S 1/2; the ionization limit is a separate 'Limit' row and in ionization_energy.

ASD levels are not isotope resolved: the compilation mixes data from different isotopes and natural samples; isotope shifts and hyperfine structure are not separated. RydState 'Li' uses mass number 7; hyperfine structure is not resolved in ASD (centroid / fine-structure energies).
Energy precision is ASD's (compilation) precision; for many Rydberg series more precise modern measurements exist (e.g. mm-wave or laser spectroscopy) and should be preferred in fits.

Column j in levels.csv is the total J of the level as given by ASD; s is the total spin from the LS term multiplicity; for jj/jK-coupled terms only n and l are assigned. n, l are filled only when the configuration has exactly one electron outside the RydState core configuration '1s2' (same rule as rydstate.species.nist.parse_nist_energy_levels).

ASD states for Li I: 'Unpublished level list prepared for line classifications published in Kelly 1987. These data are not critically evaluated by NIST.' Li I level energies are mostly given to 0.01 cm^-1 or worse.
